data.long_meaning: Sarwan is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Sarv’ meaning all, and ‘An’ meaning lord, ruler or king. Therefore, Sarwan means the ruler of all. The name Sarwan carries the meaning “King, Ruler” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Punjabi. Parents who choose Sarwan usually hope their child will grow to embody king, ruler and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Sarwan was a prominent Hindu ruler of the Sikh Empire in the late 18th century. The name Sarwan carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context:
Sarwan Singh was the seventh and last human Maharaja of the Sikh Empire, ruling from Lahore.
He was the eldest son of Ranjit Singh, who established the Sikh Empire in 1799.
Sarwan Singh succeeded his father in 1839 and ruled until his death in 1840.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Sarwan was a Hindu general under the reign of Maharaja Ranjit Singh in the 19th century. The name Sarwan carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context:
Sarwan Singh was a Hindu general in the Sikh army, known for his military prowess and loyalty to Maharaja Ranjit Singh.
He played a key role in the Battle of Mangalwadh in 1817 and was later appointed as the governor of Multan in 1822.
Sarwan Singh was a trusted advisor and commander to Ranjit Singh and played a significant role in the expansion and consolidation of the Sikh Empire.
